newsitem.title: USA: US spot heat dips in thin late trade, basis shifts.
newsitem.headline: US spot heat dips in thin late trade, basis shifts.

text.p: U.S. spot products traded quietly late Monday as market players searched out solid differentials as March NYMEX futures became the basis price.
NYMEX heating oil slipped nearly one cent lower by the close, while gasoline ended slightly higher on the day.
Traders said some shifting of gasoline positions in the U.S. Gulf kept prices there firm, though there appeared to be few new sellers in the market.
"I'm calling refiners and they're not returning my calls. It seems to be mostly the trade that's buying today," said one trader in Houston.
At the USG, conventional unleaded M4 barrels were offered at 2.50 cents under the screen for delivery on the 5th cycle of the Colonial Pipeline.
USG No. 2 oil barrels changed hands at 1.65 cents under NYMEX early in the day, traders said, though it appeared to be better bid later in the day with little material on offer.
Prompt New York Harbor (NYH) No. 2 was offered at 2.50 cents over, reflecting the difference between Friday's February NYMEX price and Monday's March NYMEX price.
News of colder temperatures expected across the Midwest and Northeast by late week failed to trigger a price hike in the spot markets, traders said.
